storyTitle: Story (From the Life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ)
story: A dispute once arose between two people, and one of them tried to present his case in a way that would make him seem right, even though he was not fully truthful. He spoke in a convincing way to win the judgment. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ listened carefully and then warned, “Perhaps some of you are more eloquent than others in presenting their case. I judge based on what I hear. If I give someone a right that belongs to his brother, then he should not take it, for it would be a portion of the Hellfire.” (Sahih al-Bukhari & Muslim) This showed that fairness is not just about winning—it is about truth. Even if someone can speak well and appear right, Allah knows the reality.
reflection: Fairness depends on truth. If truth is hidden, people may be treated unjustly. A strong believer does not support unfairness, even if it benefits them. Like the Prophet ﷺ taught, real success is not winning—it is being truthful and just. When you stand for truth, you help create fairness for everyone.
parentTip: Encourage fairness in daily situations—ask your child, “Is this fair for everyone?” so they learn to connect honesty with justice. Becoming someone others trust

title: BECOMING SOMEONE OTHERS TRUST
intro: Becoming someone others trust means being known as a person who always speaks the truth, keeps promises, and does what is right. Trust is not built in one day—it grows slowly through honest actions in small and big matters. When people see that you are truthful, they feel safe with you and rely on you. A believer does not only avoid lying—they become a person others can depend on. Allah loves those who are trustworthy and sincere.
quranText: “And they who are to their trusts and promises attentive.” (23:8)
hadithText: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: “There is no faith for the one who is not trustworthy.” (Musnad Ahmad)
storyTitle: Story (From the Life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ)
story: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was known among his people as Al-Ameen (the Trustworthy) even before he became a Prophet. People trusted him with their belongings, their decisions, and their important matters. When the Ka‘bah was being rebuilt, the tribes of Makkah disagreed about who should place the Black Stone. It became a serious conflict. They decided that the next person to enter would judge between them—and that person was Muhammad ﷺ. Because they trusted him, they all accepted his decision without argument. He placed the stone on a cloth and asked leaders from each tribe to lift it together, then he placed it in its position himself. His honesty and fairness made him a person everyone trusted.
reflection: Trust is one of the most valuable qualities a person can have. When you are honest in your words and actions, people begin to rely on you. Like the Prophet ﷺ, being truthful makes you respected and trusted by others. Trust is built step by step, through everyday honesty.
parentTip: Give your child small responsibilities and appreciate when they handle them honestly—this helps them see themselves as trustworthy individuals. Creating a habit of daily truthful reflection

title: CREATING A HABIT OF DAILY TRUTHFUL REFLECTION
intro: Creating a habit of daily truthful reflection means taking a little time every day to think honestly about your actions, words, and choices. It means asking yourself, “Was I truthful today? Did I hide anything? Could I have done better?” This habit helps you grow, improve, and stay aware of your character. A believer does not only act—they reflect, learn, and become better each day. Allah loves those who are mindful of their actions and sincere in improving themselves.
quranText: “O you who believe! Fear Allah, and let every soul look to what it has put forth for tomorrow…” (59:18)
hadithText: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: “The wise person is the one who holds himself accountable and works for what comes after death…” (Sunan al-Tirmidhi)
storyTitle: Story (From the Life of Umar ibn Al-Khattab رضي الله عنه)
story: Hazrat Umar ibn Al-Khattab رضي الله عنه was known for his strong sense of accountability. He would often say, “Take account of yourselves before you are taken to account.” Every day, he would reflect on his actions—thinking about what he did right and where he needed to improve. Even though he was a great leader, he never stopped checking himself. His honesty with himself made him just, strong, and close to Allah. He did not wait for others to correct him—he corrected himself daily.
reflection: Taking time each day to think honestly about your actions helps you become better. When you reflect, you notice your mistakes and your good deeds. Like Umar رضي الله عنه, being honest with yourself builds strong character. Small daily reflection leads to big improvement over time.
parentTip: Create a nightly habit—ask your child one simple question: “What is one truth you told today?” This builds self-awareness and love for honesty. Making honesty part of identity

title: MAKING HONESTY PART OF IDENTITY
intro: Making honesty part of your identity means becoming a person who is known for always telling the truth. It is not something you do sometimes—it becomes who you are. When honesty becomes your identity, you don’t need to think twice—you naturally choose truth in every situation. People begin to recognize you as someone trustworthy and sincere. A believer builds such a strong habit of truth that it becomes part of their character. Allah loves those who are known as truthful.
quranText: “O you who believe! Fear Allah and be with those who are truthful.” (9:119)
hadithText: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: “A man continues to speak the truth until he is recorded with Allah as a truthful person (Siddeeq).” (Sahih al-Bukhari & Muslim)
storyTitle: Story (From the Life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ)
story: In Madinah, there lived a companion whose words were always trusted and whose character reflected truth in every situation — Abu Dharr al-Ghifari. He was known for speaking honestly, even when it was difficult, even when it went against people’s expectations. One day, the Prophet ﷺ gave him sincere advice. He told him to always speak the truth, even if it was bitter, and not to fear the criticism of others when standing for what is right. This was not just guidance for a moment — it was a way of life. Abu Dharr took these words deeply into his heart. Over time, honesty was no longer something he had to think about or struggle with in each situation. It became part of who he was. Whether he was among friends, leaders, or ordinary people, his tongue did not change. He did not adjust the truth to please others, nor did he hide it to protect himself. There were times when speaking openly brought him difficulty. People did not always like hearing the truth, especially when it challenged their behavior. Yet Abu Dharr remained firm. He chose to live with honesty rather than comfort. Because of this consistency, people came to recognize him for what he stood for. His identity became tied to truthfulness. When he spoke, his words carried weight — not because they were loud, but because they were real. This shows that honesty is not just a single action; it is something that grows into a person’s identity. When someone repeatedly chooses truth in small and big moments, it becomes a natural part of them. And when honesty becomes part of who you are, it shapes your character, your relationships, and the way people trust you.
reflection: Honesty should not be something you do only sometimes—it should become who you are. When you choose truth again and again, it becomes part of your identity. Like the Prophet ﷺ, being consistently truthful makes you respected, trusted, and loved by Allah.
parentTip: Label your child positively—say “You are an honest person” instead of just praising actions, so honesty becomes part of their identity.

title: HELPING SOMEONE IN NEED
intro: Helping someone in need means noticing when someone is struggling and choosing to support them with kindness. It is not limited to giving money — it can be helping with time, effort, or even a caring word. A believer does not ignore the difficulties of others; instead, they try to ease them. When helping others becomes a habit, it builds compassion and brings people closer together. Allah loves those who care for others and respond to their needs.
quranText: “Have you seen the one who denies the religion? That is the one who repulses the orphan and does not encourage the feeding of the poor.” (107:1–3)
hadithText: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: “The most beloved people to Allah are those who are most beneficial to people.” (Reported in al-Mu‘jam al-Awsat)
storyTitle: Story (From the Life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ)
story: In Madinah, there lived a woman who had no one to rely on. She was weak and struggled to manage her daily needs. Life was not easy for her, and even small tasks felt heavy. The Prophet ﷺ, despite carrying the responsibility of leading a community, did not overlook people like her. One day, she approached him with a simple request for help. Without hesitation, Prophet Muhammad responded with humility and kindness. He did not send someone else in his place, nor did he make her feel unimportant. Instead, he told her gently to take him wherever she needed, and he walked with her through the streets of Madinah until her need was fulfilled. There was no pride in his actions, no display of status — only sincere care. He gave his time and attention as if her need was the most important matter at that moment. For the woman, it was more than just help; it was dignity, respect, and relief. This moment showed the companions that helping others is not about how big the act is, but about the sincerity behind it. Even the greatest leader did not consider any act of helping too small.
reflection: Helping someone in need is a sign of a caring heart. When you notice others and support them, even in small ways, you spread kindness and bring ease into someone’s life.
parentTip: Encourage children to look for small ways to help at home or outside, like assisting a sibling or helping a classmate. Praise the effort so they begin to enjoy helping others.

title: SHARING FOOD WITH OTHERS
intro: Sharing food with others means caring about people around you and not keeping everything for yourself. It teaches kindness, generosity, and love. Even if the food is little, sharing it brings blessings and strengthens relationships. A believer thinks about others, especially those who may not have enough, and happily includes them. Allah loves those who feed others and care for the hungry.
quranText: “And they give food, in spite of love for it, to the needy, the orphan, and the captive.” (76:8)
hadithText: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: “O young boy, mention the name of Allah, eat with your right hand, and eat from what is near you.” (Sahih al-Bukhari & Muslim) He also taught sharing and said: “The food of two is enough for three, and the food of three is enough for four.” (Sahih al-Bukhari & Muslim)
storyTitle: Story (From the Life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ)
story: In Madinah, there came a time when a guest arrived to meet the Prophet ﷺ. The guest was hungry, and the Prophet ﷺ wished to host him, but there was very little food available in his home. He asked if anyone among the companions could take the guest and care for him. A companion from the Ansar stepped forward and took the guest to his house. When he arrived, he found that there was only a small amount of food — just enough for his children. He and his wife quietly spoke to each other and decided to give priority to their guest. They put the children to sleep and prepared the food. When it was time to eat, they dimmed the lamp and sat with the guest, pretending to eat so that he would feel comfortable. In reality, they stayed hungry while the guest ate fully, not letting him feel that he was taking their share. The next day, when this reached Prophet Muhammad, he appreciated what they had done. Their act of sharing, even in hardship, was loved by Allah. This moment showed that sharing food is not about having extra — it is about having a generous heart. Even when there is little, choosing to give can bring great reward and strengthen bonds between people.
reflection: Sharing food brings hearts closer. Even a small meal, when shared, becomes full of blessings and love.
parentTip: Encourage children to share snacks with siblings or friends. Occasionally let them divide food themselves so they learn fairness and generosity together.

title: COMFORTING A SAD FRIEND
intro: Comforting a sad friend means noticing when someone is hurt or upset and trying to bring them ease with kindness. It can be through gentle words, sitting beside them, or simply showing that you care. A believer does not ignore the sadness of others; instead, they try to bring comfort and hope. When we support others in their difficult moments, we strengthen friendship and spread mercy. Allah loves those who care for the feelings of others.
quranText: “The believers are but brothers, so make peace between your brothers…” (49:10)
hadithText: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: “The example of the believers in their mutual love, mercy, and compassion is like one body; when one part of it feels pain, the whole body responds with sleeplessness and fever.” (Sahih al-Bukhari & Muslim)
storyTitle: Story (From the Life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ)
story: In Madinah, a young boy would often bring joy to gatherings with his cheerful presence. His name was Abu Umayr, and he had a small bird that he loved dearly. He would play with it and care for it every day. One day, the Prophet ﷺ noticed that the boy was unusually quiet and sad. His usual smile was gone. The Prophet ﷺ did not ignore this change. Instead, he gently came close to him and spoke in a soft, caring tone, “O Abu Umayr, what happened to the little bird?” The bird had died, and the child’s heart was heavy with loss. The Prophet ﷺ did not give a long lecture or dismiss his feelings as something small. Instead, he acknowledged his sadness in a simple and kind way. By mentioning the bird, he showed the child that his feelings mattered. That gentle moment brought comfort to the boy. He felt seen, understood, and cared for. The Prophet ﷺ, despite carrying the responsibility of an entire community, took time to ease the sadness of a child. Through this, Prophet Muhammad taught that comforting someone does not always require big actions. Sometimes, a kind word, a soft tone, and sincere attention are enough to heal a hurting heart.
reflection: When a friend is sad, your kindness can bring them comfort. Even small words or actions can make a big difference in how someone feels.
parentTip: Teach children to notice emotions by asking, “How can we make them feel better?” Encourage simple actions like sitting with a friend, sharing kind words, or offering help.

title: SPEAKING GENTLY TO OTHERS
intro: Speaking gently to others means choosing kind, soft, and respectful words when talking to people. It is not only what you say, but how you say it that matters. Gentle speech makes others feel safe, valued, and respected, while harsh words can hurt hearts and push people away. A believer controls their tone and speaks with kindness, even when they are upset. Allah loves those who speak with gentleness and wisdom.
quranText: “And speak to him with gentle speech that perhaps he may be reminded or fear Allah.” (20:44)
hadithText: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: “Gentleness is not found in anything except that it beautifies it, and it is not removed from anything except that it makes it defective.” (Sahih Muslim)
storyTitle: Story (From the Life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ)
story: In Madinah, a man once came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked for permission to commit a sinful act. The request shocked the people around him, and some companions became upset at hearing such words. It was not something that was normally spoken about openly. But instead of reacting harshly, Prophet Muhammad called the young man closer and spoke to him calmly. He did not embarrass him or push him away. Instead, he gently asked him a question, “Would you like this for your mother?” The young man immediately said no. Then the Prophet ﷺ continued, asking about his daughter, his sister, and other close relations. Each time, the young man responded that he would not want such a thing for them. Through these gentle questions, the Prophet ﷺ helped him understand the wrong in a way that touched his heart. There was no shouting, no anger — only calm and caring words that guided him to the truth. By the end of the conversation, the young man’s thinking had changed. What began as a shocking request turned into a moment of guidance, simply because it was handled with gentleness. This showed the companions that soft speech has a powerful effect. When words are kind, they open hearts. When they are harsh, they close them. The Prophet ﷺ led by example, teaching that even difficult conversations should be carried with gentleness.
reflection: Gentle words make others feel respected and understood. When you speak kindly, people are more likely to listen and respond positively.
parentTip: Model gentle speech at home. When correcting children, lower your tone instead of raising it — children learn how to speak by how they are spoken to.

title: CARING FOR YOUNGER SIBLINGS
intro: Caring for younger siblings means showing kindness, patience, and responsibility toward those who are younger than you. It includes helping them, protecting them, and treating them with love. A believer understands that being older is not about control, but about care and support. When you look after younger ones with a gentle heart, you build strong bonds and earn reward from Allah. Allah loves those who show mercy to others, especially those who are younger and depend on us.
quranText: “And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy…” (17:24)
hadithText: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: “He is not one of us who does not show mercy to our young and respect to our elders.” (Sunan al-Tirmidhi)
storyTitle: Story (From the Life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ)
story: In Madinah, the Prophet ﷺ would often spend time with children, treating them with kindness and affection. Among them was his beloved grandson, Hasan ibn Ali, who was still very young. One day, Hasan (RA) picked up a date from the charity dates and placed it in his mouth. For a child, it seemed like a small and innocent action. But the Prophet ﷺ immediately noticed. He gently removed the date from his mouth and said, “Do you not know that we do not eat from charity?” There was no harshness in his voice, no anger in his action. Instead, there was care, teaching, and protection. He was guiding the child with love, ensuring he learned what was right from a young age. In other moments, the Prophet ﷺ would carry his grandsons, play with them, and show them affection openly. He did not ignore them or treat them as unimportant. He gave them attention, taught them gently, and cared for their growth. Through this, Prophet Muhammad showed that caring for younger ones means more than just helping them — it means guiding them with patience, protecting them from wrong, and showing them love.
reflection: Younger siblings look up to you. When you treat them with kindness and patience, you help them grow with love and confidence.
parentTip: Encourage older children to take small responsibilities for younger siblings, like helping them or guiding them gently. Appreciate their care so they begin to value this role positively.

title: SHOWING KINDNESS TO ANIMALS
intro: Showing kindness to animals means treating them with care, mercy, and respect. Animals cannot speak for themselves, but they feel hunger, pain, and fear just like humans. A believer understands that all creatures are created by Allah and deserve to be treated gently. Being kind to animals includes feeding them, not hurting them, and taking care of them when they are weak. Allah loves those who show mercy to every living being.
quranText: “There is no creature on earth or bird that flies with its wings except that they are communities like you…” (6:38)
hadithText: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: “In every living being there is reward.” (Sahih al-Bukhari & Muslim)
storyTitle: Story (From the Life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ)
story: During one of the journeys, the companions of the Prophet ﷺ came across a bird and its small chicks. They picked up the chicks, and the mother bird began to fly above them in distress, flapping her wings anxiously. She could not speak, but her fear and pain were clear. When Prophet Muhammad saw this, he immediately noticed the bird’s condition. He asked, “Who has distressed this bird by taking its young?” His voice carried concern, not just instruction. The companions quickly realized their mistake. They returned the chicks to their place, and the bird calmed down. The situation was simple, but the lesson was deep. The Prophet ﷺ did not ignore the suffering of an animal, even for a moment. He taught that causing fear or harm to any living creature is wrong, and that kindness should extend beyond humans. Through this, the companions learned that mercy is not limited — it includes every living being. Even a small bird deserves care and protection.
reflection: Kindness is not only for people — it is for all living creatures. When you treat animals gently, you show a merciful and caring heart.
parentTip: Teach children to be gentle with animals by guiding their actions. If they see an animal, encourage calm behavior and explain how animals feel, helping them build empathy from a young age.

title: SMILING AS AN ACT OF KINDNESS
intro: Smiling as an act of kindness means showing warmth and friendliness through a simple expression. A smile can make others feel welcomed, valued, and at ease. It does not cost anything, yet it can brighten someone’s day and remove discomfort from hearts. A believer understands that even small acts of kindness carry great reward, and a smile is one of the easiest ways to spread goodness. Allah loves those who bring ease and happiness to others.
quranText: عمران “So by mercy from Allah, you were gentle with them…” (3:159)
hadithText: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: “Your smile in the face of your brother is charity.” (Sunan al-Tirmidhi)
storyTitle: Story (From the Life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ)
story: In Madinah, the companions closely observed not only what the Prophet ﷺ said, but how he behaved in everyday life. Among those who witnessed his character was Abdullah ibn al-Harith, who later described something simple yet powerful. He said that he never saw anyone who smiled more than the Prophet ﷺ. His smile was not forced or occasional — it was a natural part of his character. Whether he met children, companions, or even those who were new to Islam, he would greet them with a pleasant face. His smile made people feel comfortable around him. Those who were nervous felt at ease, and those who were distant felt welcomed. It was not just an expression; it was a way of spreading kindness without words. Even in moments of responsibility and seriousness, the Prophet ﷺ did not lose this gentle habit. His smile carried warmth, showing people that kindness can exist alongside strength and leadership. Through this, Prophet Muhammad taught that small actions can have a big impact. A simple smile can lift hearts, build connections, and bring people closer.
reflection: A smile is a small act, but it can make a big difference. It spreads kindness and makes others feel happy and comfortable.
parentTip: Encourage children to greet family members and others with a smile. Model this behavior at home so they naturally adopt it in their daily interactions.

title: AVOIDING HURTFUL WORDS
intro: Avoiding hurtful words means choosing to speak in a way that does not harm others. Words can leave deep marks on the heart, even if they are said in anger or as a joke. A believer thinks before speaking and avoids language that insults, mocks, or hurts feelings. Instead, they choose words that are kind, respectful, and beneficial. Allah loves those who protect others from harm — even through their speech.
quranText: “O you who believe! Let not one group mock another…” (49:11)
hadithText: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: “Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak good or remain silent.” (Sahih al-Bukhari & Muslim)
storyTitle: Story (From the Life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ)
story: In Madinah, a companion once spoke words about another person that were not kind. It may have seemed small at the moment, but those words carried hurt. When the Prophet ﷺ came to know about it, he did not ignore it. He gently explained the seriousness of such speech. He told them that speaking negatively about someone, even if it is true, is like harming them in their absence. He made them understand this in a way that touched their hearts, comparing it to something so unpleasant that it made them realize the weight of their words. The companions were deeply affected. What they once thought was a small comment now felt heavy. They understood that words are not just sounds — they carry impact, and they can hurt people even when they are not present. Through this moment, Prophet Muhammad taught them to guard their tongues. He showed that avoiding hurtful words is not just good manners — it is part of faith.
reflection: Words can hurt more than we realize. Choosing kind speech protects others and keeps your heart clean.
parentTip: Teach children to pause before speaking by asking, “Will this make someone feel good or bad?” This simple habit helps them become more thoughtful with their words.

title: IDENTIFYING BULLYING BEHAVIOR
intro: Identifying bullying behavior means recognizing actions that hurt, scare, or make others feel small. Bullying can be through words, actions, or exclusion — like teasing, mocking, pushing, or leaving someone out on purpose. A believer does not ignore such behavior; they understand that hurting others is ظلم (wrongdoing). When you can identify bullying, you are better able to stop it, stand for what is right, and protect those who are being hurt. Allah does not love those who harm others.
quranText: “O you who believe! Let not one group mock another…” (49:11)
hadithText: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: “A Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand other Muslims are safe.” (Sahih al-Bukhari & Muslim)
storyTitle: Story (From the Life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ)
story: In Madinah, there were moments when some companions would say things in a light or joking manner, not realizing that their words could hurt others. On one such occasion, a remark was made about the appearance of another companion. It may have seemed small to the one who said it, but it carried hurt. When the Prophet ﷺ came to know about it, he did not ignore it. He addressed it immediately, making it clear that looking down on someone or mocking them is not acceptable. He reminded them that all people have dignity and honor, and no one should be made to feel less because of how they look or who they are. His correction was firm but wise. It helped them recognize that what might feel like a joke can actually be harmful. Through this, Prophet Muhammad taught them to become aware of their behavior and its impact on others. The companions learned to be more careful with their words and actions. They began to understand that bullying is not always loud or obvious — sometimes it hides in small comments or careless behavior.
reflection: Bullying can be in words, actions, or even silence. When you recognize it, you can choose to stop it and stand for kindness.
parentTip: Help children identify bullying by discussing real-life examples. Ask questions like, “How would you feel if someone said that to you?” to build awareness and empathy.

title: SEEING WHEN SOMEONE IS LEFT OUT
intro: Seeing when someone is left out means noticing when a person is alone, ignored, or not included by others. It requires awareness and a caring heart. A believer does not only focus on themselves or their friends, but also looks around to see who might be feeling left out. Including others, especially those who are alone, brings comfort and builds strong bonds. Allah loves those who care for others and make them feel valued.
quranText: “Worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, and be good to parents, relatives, orphans, the needy…” (4:36)
hadithText: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: “The believer to the believer is like a building, each part supporting the other.” (Sahih al-Bukhari & Muslim)
storyTitle: Story (From the Life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ)
story: In Madinah, there was a companion who was not strong in status or appearance, but he was loved for his sincerity. His name was Julaybib. Many people would often overlook him, and he did not have the same social standing as others. In gatherings, he could easily be left unnoticed. But the Prophet ﷺ did not see him the way others did. He noticed him, valued him, and brought him close. One day, the Prophet ﷺ even took a personal interest in helping him find a place in society and encouraged his marriage, showing the community that he was worthy of respect and inclusion. Later, after a battle, the Prophet ﷺ asked the companions, “Is anyone missing?” They mentioned a few names, but no one mentioned Julaybib. Then the Prophet ﷺ said, “But I am missing Julaybib.” He personally went to search for him and found that he had been martyred. The Prophet ﷺ stood by him with care and said words that honored him, showing his deep concern for someone others often overlooked. Through this, Prophet Muhammad taught the companions to notice those who are left out. He showed that every person matters, even if others do not pay attention to them.
reflection: Sometimes people feel left out quietly. When you notice and include them, you make them feel valued and happy.
parentTip: Encourage children to look around during play or group activities and invite someone who is alone. Praise this behavior so it becomes a natural habit.

title: IDENTIFYING HARSH SPEECH
intro: Identifying harsh speech means recognizing words or tones that hurt, insult, or make others feel uncomfortable. Harsh speech is not only about what is said, but also how it is said. Sometimes a person may speak loudly, angrily, or disrespectfully, causing pain to others. A believer is aware of this and learns to notice when speech becomes rough or hurtful. By identifying it, one can correct it and choose kindness instead. Allah loves those who speak gently and avoid hurting others with their words.
quranText: “And do not insult one another and do not call each other by offensive nicknames…” (49:11)
hadithText: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: “The strong person is not the one who overcomes others by strength, but the one who controls himself while in anger.” (Sahih al-Bukhari & Muslim)
storyTitle: Story (From the Life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ)
story: In Madinah, a man once came to the Prophet ﷺ asking for advice. He did not ask for many things — just something simple that he could hold onto. The Prophet ﷺ looked at him and said, “Do not become angry.” The man repeated his request several times, and each time, the Prophet ﷺ gave him the same answer. This was not just about anger itself, but about what anger leads to, especially harsh speech. When a person becomes angry, their words often become rough, hurtful, and uncontrolled. Through this simple but repeated advice, Prophet Muhammad was teaching him to recognize the beginning of harsh behavior. If a person can identify the moment anger rises, they can stop themselves before their words hurt others. The companions understood that controlling speech begins with awareness. If you notice when your tone is changing or your words are becoming sharp, you can pause and choose better words.
reflection: Harsh speech often starts with anger. When you recognize it early, you can stop it and choose kind words instead.
parentTip: Teach children to recognize their tone by asking, “Does your voice sound kind or angry?” Helping them notice this early builds self-control over speech.

title: RECOGNIZING SELFISHNESS
intro: Recognizing selfishness means understanding when a person is thinking only about themselves and ignoring the needs of others. It can appear in small ways, like not sharing, always wanting more, or not caring how others feel. A believer learns to notice these signs within themselves and correct them. Islam teaches us to think beyond our own needs and to care for others with sincerity. Allah loves those who are generous and considerate, not those who are selfish.
quranText: “And those who are saved from the greed of their own souls — it is they who will be successful.” (59:9)
hadithText: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: “None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.” (Sahih al-Bukhari & Muslim)
storyTitle: Story (From the Life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ)
story: In Madinah, a guest once came to the Prophet ﷺ seeking food. There was very little available in his home, so he asked if any of the companions could take the guest and care for him. One of the Ansar stood up and took the guest to his house. When he reached home, he realized there was only a small amount of food — just enough for his children. For a moment, he could have chosen to keep it for himself and his family. No one would have known. But instead, he and his wife made a different decision. They put the children to sleep and prepared the food for their guest. To make the guest feel comfortable, they dimmed the lamp and pretended to eat with him, while in reality they remained hungry. The guest ate fully, unaware that his hosts had given up their own share. The next day, when this reached Prophet Muhammad, he appreciated their action. They had overcome their own need and chose to care for someone else instead. This moment shows the opposite of selfishness. While selfishness focuses only on “me,” true belief teaches “others before me.” Recognizing selfishness begins by noticing these choices — when we have the chance to keep everything for ourselves, or to share and care for others.
reflection: Selfishness makes us think only about ourselves. When you notice it and choose to share instead, you grow into a more caring and generous person.
parentTip: Create situations where children can practice sharing, like dividing treats among siblings. Guide them to think about others’ feelings so they learn to overcome selfishness naturally.

title: NOTICING UNFAIR TREATMENT
intro: Noticing unfair treatment means being aware when someone is not being treated justly or equally. It could be when someone is given less, ignored, or treated wrongly compared to others. A believer does not ignore ظلم (injustice), even in small matters. Instead, they become aware of it and feel concerned. Recognizing unfairness is the first step toward standing for justice and helping others. Allah loves those who are fair and aware of the rights of others.
quranText: “O you who believe! Stand firmly for justice…” (4:135)
hadithText: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: “Help your brother, whether he is an oppressor or oppressed.” The companions asked, “O Messenger of Allah, we help the oppressed, but how do we help the oppressor?” He replied, “By stopping him from oppression.” (Sahih al-Bukhari)
storyTitle: Story (From the Life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ)
story: In Madinah, during the early days of the Muslim community, a situation arose where a person from a weaker background was treated unfairly, while someone from a stronger group was being defended despite being in the wrong. People began to lean toward supporting their own side instead of looking at what was truly right. When the matter reached the Prophet ﷺ, he did not allow status or background to influence judgment. Prophet Muhammad made it clear that justice does not change based on who a person is. What is wrong remains wrong, no matter who does it. On another occasion, he emphasized this principle strongly by saying that even if someone very close to him were to do wrong, they would still be held accountable. This showed the companions that fairness is not selective, it is consistent. Through this, the companions learned to notice unfair treatment, even when it involved people they knew or liked. They understood that being just means looking beyond personal connections and standing with what is right.
reflection: Unfair treatment can happen in small and big ways. When you notice it, you can choose to stand for what is right and support fairness.
parentTip: Discuss everyday situations with children, like sharing or taking turns, and ask, “Was that fair?” This helps them develop a natural sense of justice and awareness.

title: BEING KIND WHEN OTHERS ARE NOT
intro: Being kind when others are not means choosing good behavior even when people around you are rude, unfair, or unkind. It is easy to respond with the same negativity, but a believer controls their actions and responds with patience and kindness. This shows strength of character and trust in Allah. Kindness in difficult moments has a powerful impact, it can soften hearts and change situations. Allah loves those who repay bad with good.
quranText: “Repel evil with that which is better…” (41:34)
hadithText: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: “The strong person is not the one who overcomes others by strength, but the one who controls himself while in anger.” (Sahih al-Bukhari & Muslim)
storyTitle: Story (From the Life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ)
story: In Makkah, during the early days of Islam, the Prophet ﷺ faced harsh treatment from his people. They rejected his message, mocked him, and at times even harmed him. On one occasion, while he was walking through the streets, someone threw dirt on him. It was a moment that could have easily led to anger or retaliation. Instead, Prophet Muhammad quietly returned home. His daughter cleaned him with care, feeling hurt at what had happened. Yet the Prophet ﷺ did not respond with harsh words or revenge. He remained patient and continued to show kindness, even to those who treated him badly. In another instance, when he went to the city of Ta’if to invite people to truth, he was rejected in a painful way. People threw stones at him until he was injured. Despite this, when given the chance to respond against them, he chose mercy instead. He hoped that goodness would come from them or their future generations. Through these moments, the Prophet ﷺ showed that kindness is not dependent on how others behave. It is a choice that comes from within. Even when others were not kind, he did not lower his character. Instead, he remained gentle, patient, and hopeful.
reflection: Kindness is strongest when it is shown in difficult moments. When others are not kind, your good behavior can make a real difference.
parentTip: Teach children not to react immediately when treated unfairly. Encourage them to pause and respond with calm words, helping them build emotional strength and kindness.

title: DEFENDING SOMEONE UNFAIRLY TREATED
intro: Defending someone who is unfairly treated means standing beside a person who is being wronged and helping them receive justice. It requires courage to speak or act when others remain silent. A believer does not ignore ظلم, whether it is big or small, but supports the one who is oppressed in a wise and fair way. Allah loves those who stand for truth and protect the rights of others.
quranText: “Indeed, We have revealed to you the Book in truth so that you may judge between people by what Allah has shown you, and do not be an advocate for the deceitful.” (4:105)
hadithText: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: “Help your brother, whether he is an oppressor or oppressed.” The companions asked, “O Messenger of Allah, we help the oppressed, but how do we help the oppressor?” He replied, “By stopping him from oppression.” (Sahih al-Bukhari)
storyTitle: Story (From the Life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ)
story: In Madinah, a Jewish man once came forward with a complaint. His armor had been stolen, and suspicion fell on a Muslim man. Instead of admitting his mistake, the man tried to shift the blame onto the Jewish neighbor, hoping people would support him simply because he was from among them. As the matter spread, some people began speaking in favor of the Muslim, not because he was right, but because of loyalty. The Jewish man stood alone, at risk of losing his right without anyone to defend him. When the case reached Prophet Muhammad, he did not take sides based on identity. He listened carefully and waited for the truth to become clear. Then Allah revealed guidance exposing the reality, that the Muslim man was at fault and the Jewish man was innocent. Without hesitation, the Prophet ﷺ stood firmly with the truth and defended the one who had been wronged, even though he was not from the Muslim community. Justice was restored, and the false accusation was corrected.
reflection: Standing for someone who is treated unfairly shows true courage. Justice is not about who a person is, but about what is right.
parentTip: Teach children that fairness applies to everyone. Encourage them to support what is right, even if it means not siding with their own friends.

title: SHOWING MERCY IN ANGER
intro: Showing mercy in anger means controlling yourself when you feel upset and choosing kindness instead of reacting harshly. Anger is a natural feeling, but how you respond to it shows your character. A believer does not let anger lead to hurtful words or actions. Instead, they pause, forgive, and show mercy. Allah loves those who control their anger and treat others with patience.
quranText: عمران “…and those who restrain anger and pardon people…” (3:134)
hadithText: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: “The strong person is not the one who overcomes others by strength, but the one who controls himself while in anger.” (Sahih al-Bukhari & Muslim)
storyTitle: Story (From the Life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ)
story: In Madinah, Anas ibn Malik served the Prophet ﷺ for many years. During this time, he carried out many small tasks, as young helpers often do. Like any child, there were moments when he made mistakes or did not complete something as expected. On one occasion, Anas (RA) had gone to do a task but became distracted and delayed. Time passed, and the Prophet ﷺ came looking for him. When he found him, Anas felt nervous, expecting to be scolded. But the Prophet ﷺ did not respond with anger. Instead, he simply smiled gently and said a few soft words, without harshness or blame. There was no shouting, no punishment, and no hurtful reaction. Anas later said that throughout all the years he served the Prophet ﷺ, he never once heard him say, “Why did you do this?” or “Why did you not do that?” Through this, Prophet Muhammad showed that even when mistakes happen and anger could arise, mercy is stronger. He chose patience over reaction, and kindness over harshness.
reflection: When you feel angry, you have a choice. Showing mercy instead of reacting harshly makes you stronger and more respected.
parentTip: Teach children simple calming steps, like pausing or taking a breath before responding. Model calm behavior so they learn to handle anger with patience and mercy.

title: CHOOSING KINDNESS OVER REVENGE
intro: Choosing kindness over revenge means letting go of the desire to hurt someone back when they have wronged you. It is natural to feel upset, but a believer rises above that feeling and responds with forgiveness and goodness. Revenge may feel satisfying for a moment, but kindness brings lasting peace and earns the pleasure of Allah. Allah loves those who forgive and respond with what is better.
quranText: “Repel evil with that which is better…” (41:34)
hadithText: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: “The merciful are shown mercy by the Most Merciful. Be merciful to those on the earth and the One above the heavens will have mercy upon you.” (Sunan al-Tirmidhi)
storyTitle: Story (From the Life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ)
story: After many years of hardship, the Prophet ﷺ returned to Makkah with strength and support. This was the city where he had been rejected, mocked, and harmed. Many of the same people who once hurt him were now standing before him, fearful of what might happen next. They remembered how they had treated him and expected that this moment would bring revenge. The power was now in his hands, and he could have chosen to respond in the same way they had treated him. But instead, Prophet Muhammad stood before them with calmness and dignity. He asked them what they thought he would do to them. They replied with hope, calling him a noble brother and the son of a noble brother. At that moment, he said words that changed everything: “No blame will be upon you today.” He chose forgiveness over revenge, kindness over punishment. The people who once expected harshness were met with mercy. This act softened hearts and opened the way for many to accept the truth. This moment showed that true strength is not in taking revenge, but in rising above it. When kindness replaces anger, it has the power to transform even the hardest hearts.
reflection: Choosing kindness instead of revenge brings peace and strength. It shows true character and can change others for the better.
parentTip: Teach children that when someone hurts them, they can choose to respond calmly instead of reacting. Encourage phrases like, “I forgive you,” to build emotional strength and kindness.

title: SPEAKING GENTLY IN CONFLICT
intro: Speaking gently in conflict means choosing calm, respectful, and kind words even when there is disagreement. It is easy to raise your voice or become harsh during arguments, but a believer controls their tone and speaks with wisdom. Gentle speech helps calm situations, while harsh words make them worse. Allah loves those who handle conflicts with patience and kindness.
quranText: “And speak to him with gentle speech that perhaps he may be reminded or fear Allah.” (20:44)
hadithText: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: “Gentleness is not found in anything except that it beautifies it, and it is not removed from anything except that it makes it defective.” (Sahih Muslim)
storyTitle: Story (From the Life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ)
story: In Madinah, a man once came to the Prophet ﷺ with a harsh tone, demanding his right in a way that surprised those around him. His words were not soft, and his manner could have easily led to a strong reaction. The companions felt upset and wanted to respond to him firmly. But Prophet Muhammad immediately stopped them. He understood that the man was speaking out of frustration, not disrespect. Instead of replying with harshness, the Prophet ﷺ spoke gently and calmly to him. He said that the one who has a right may speak, and then he instructed that the man’s need be fulfilled in a good manner. There was no anger in his voice, no harsh reply — only fairness and gentleness. The situation, which could have turned into conflict, was resolved peacefully. The man’s tension eased, and the companions witnessed how calm words can control a difficult moment. Through this, the Prophet ﷺ showed that even in conflict, gentleness has power. Speaking softly does not weaken a person; it strengthens them and brings better outcomes.
reflection: In moments of conflict, your tone matters. Gentle words can calm the situation and lead to better understanding.
parentTip: Teach children to use calm phrases during disagreements, like “Let’s talk about it” or “I don’t like that.” Practice these at home so they become natural in real situations.

title: CONTROLLING HARSH REACTIONS
intro: Controlling harsh reactions means holding back from responding with anger, shouting, or hurtful actions when something upsets you. It is natural to feel angry, but a believer learns to pause and respond with patience instead of reacting quickly. Harsh reactions can damage relationships, while calm responses bring respect and peace. Allah loves those who control themselves and act with wisdom.
quranText: عمران “…and those who restrain anger and pardon people…” (3:134)
hadithText: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: “The strong person is not the one who overcomes others by strength, but the one who controls himself while in anger.” (Sahih al-Bukhari & Muslim)
storyTitle: Story (From the Life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ)
story: In Madinah, a Bedouin once came to the Prophet ﷺ and spoke in a rough and demanding manner. He pulled the Prophet’s cloak so strongly that it left a mark on his neck. The companions were upset when they saw this and felt that such behavior deserved a strong response. But instead of reacting harshly, Prophet Muhammad turned toward the man with calmness. There was no anger in his face, no raised voice, and no harsh reply. Instead, he smiled and listened to what the man wanted. The man was asking for help, and despite his rough behavior, the Prophet ﷺ ordered that he be given what he needed. The situation, which could have easily turned into conflict, ended with calmness and generosity. The companions witnessed something powerful that day. Even when treated roughly, the Prophet ﷺ controlled his reaction. He did not allow anger to take over, and he chose patience instead. Through this, they learned that true strength is not in reacting quickly, but in controlling oneself. Harsh reactions may come easily, but controlling them requires character and faith.
reflection: When you feel upset, pause before reacting. Controlling your response helps you make better choices and keeps situations calm.
parentTip: Teach children a simple pause technique, like counting to three before responding. This helps them slow down and avoid reacting harshly in emotional moments.

title: NOT CHEATING IN GAMES
intro: Not cheating in games means playing fairly and honestly, even when you really want to win. It can be tempting to bend the rules, hide mistakes, or take unfair advantage, especially when no one is watching. But a believer knows that true success is not just winning, it is doing what is right. Playing honestly builds trust, respect, and strong character. Allah loves those who are truthful in all situations, even in small things like games.
quranText: “Woe to those who give less [than due], who when they take a measure from people take in full, but when they give by measure or weight, they give less.” (83:1–3)
hadithText: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: “Whoever deceives us is not from us.” (Sahih Muslim)
storyTitle: Story (From the Life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ)
story: In Madinah, the marketplace was a place where people bought and sold goods every day. It was also a place where honesty was tested. On one occasion, the Prophet ﷺ passed by a seller who had displayed a pile of grain. From the outside, it looked dry and of good quality. As Prophet Muhammad examined it, he placed his hand inside the pile and found that the grain underneath was wet. The seller had placed the good grain on top to make it look better, hiding the lower quality beneath. The Prophet ﷺ gently asked about it, and the man explained that rain had affected it. The explanation may have been true, but hiding it was not fair. The buyer was not being given the full truth. The Prophet ﷺ then said, “Why did you not place the wet grain on top so people could see it? Whoever deceives us is not from us.” This moment showed that even small acts of dishonesty are not acceptable. Whether in trade or in play, hiding the truth to gain an advantage is a form of cheating.
reflection: Winning is not as important as being honest. Playing fairly makes you respected and trusted by others.
parentTip: Play games with children and gently reinforce fair play. If they make a mistake, guide them to admit it instead of hiding it, so honesty becomes more important than winning.

title: FOLLOWING RULES HONESTLY
intro: Following rules honestly means respecting and obeying rules even when no one is watching. Rules are made to create fairness, safety, and order. A believer does not try to break or bend them for personal benefit. Instead, they follow them with sincerity, knowing that Allah sees everything. When a person follows rules honestly, it builds trust, discipline, and strong character. Allah loves those who are truthful and consistent in their actions.
quranText: “O you who believe! Fulfill your promises…” (5:1)
hadithText: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: “The signs of a hypocrite are three: when he speaks, he lies, when he promises, he breaks it, and when he is entrusted, he betrays the trust.” (Sahih al-Bukhari & Muslim)
storyTitle: Story (From the Life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ)
story: After the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, an agreement was made between the Muslims and the Quraysh. One of its conditions was that if anyone from Makkah came to Madinah without permission from their guardians, they would be returned. Soon after the treaty was signed, a man named Abu Jandal ibn Suhayl arrived in chains, having escaped from Makkah. He was a believer who had suffered greatly and came seeking safety. Seeing him in that condition deeply affected the companions, and they wished to protect him. However, the agreement had already been made. Even though it was a painful moment, Prophet Muhammad did not break the rule. He honored the agreement and returned Abu Jandal, trusting that Allah would make a way for him. The companions found this difficult, but they learned something powerful. Following rules is not only when it is easy, but also when it is hard. The Prophet ﷺ showed that honesty in agreements is part of faith.
reflection: Following rules honestly builds trust and fairness. Even when it feels difficult, doing what is right makes you stronger in character.
parentTip: Set clear rules at home and encourage children to follow them even when unsupervised. Appreciate honesty more than perfection so they value doing right over getting away with mistakes.

title: RESPECTING OTHERS’ RIGHTS
intro: Respecting others’ rights means giving people what belongs to them and not taking or using anything unfairly. It includes respecting their property, their space, their time, and their dignity. A believer understands that every person has rights, and ignoring them leads to injustice. When we respect others’ rights, we build trust, fairness, and strong relationships. Allah loves those who are just and who return what belongs to others.
quranText: “Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to whom they are due…” (4:58)
hadithText: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: “Give the worker his wages before his sweat dries.” (Sunan Ibn Majah)
storyTitle: Story (From the Life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ)
story: Before the migration to Madinah, many people in Makkah used to leave their valuables with the Prophet ﷺ because they trusted him completely. Even those who did not believe in him still relied on his honesty and would entrust him with their belongings. When the time came for the Prophet ﷺ to leave Makkah, the situation was dangerous. His enemies were planning against him, and he had to depart secretly. Yet, despite this, he did not ignore the trusts that people had left with him. Before leaving, Prophet Muhammad asked Ali ibn Abi Talib to stay behind and return all the items to their rightful owners. These were the same people who were opposing him, yet their rights were still respected. Ali (RA) remained in Makkah and carefully returned each trust. Nothing was kept, nothing was delayed, and everyone received what belonged to them. This moment showed that respecting others’ rights is not based on how they treat you. It is based on your own character. Even in a difficult situation, the Prophet ﷺ ensured that every trust was fulfilled.
reflection: Respecting others’ rights builds fairness and trust. When you give people what belongs to them, you show honesty and strong character.
parentTip: Teach children to respect others’ belongings by asking permission before using anything. Reinforce this by appreciating when they return items properly and take care of what is not theirs.

title: RECOGNIZING BIAS
intro: Recognizing bias means understanding when someone is being treated differently not because of what is right, but because of personal preference, friendship, status, or background. Bias can make a person support someone even when they are wrong, or ignore someone’s rights because they are not part of their group. A believer learns to notice this and correct it within themselves. Islam teaches fairness for everyone, not just for those we like. Allah loves those who remain just, even when it is difficult.
quranText: “O you who believe! Stand firmly for Allah as witnesses in justice, and do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just…” (5:8)
hadithText: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: “Whoever calls to tribalism is not from us.” (Sunan Abi Dawood)
storyTitle: Story (From the Life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ)
story: In Madinah, a case once arose where a crime had been committed, and the person responsible belonged to a respected and influential family. As the matter spread, some people began to feel uncomfortable. They feared that if the punishment was carried out, it might affect the honor of that family. Because of this, they tried to find a way to avoid the consequence. They even sent Usama ibn Zayd, who was beloved to the Prophet ﷺ, to speak on behalf of the person and request leniency. When this reached Prophet Muhammad, he became serious. He understood that this was not just about one person, it was about justice itself. If rules changed based on who someone was, then fairness would be lost. He said that the nations before were destroyed because they allowed the powerful to escape punishment while holding the weak accountable. Then he made it clear that even if someone very close to him were in that position, the same rule would apply. In that moment, the companions realized how bias can influence decisions. They learned that true justice requires looking beyond relationships, status, and emotions.
reflection: Bias can make us unfair without realizing it. When you notice it and choose justice instead, you become a fair and trustworthy person.
parentTip: When children take sides, ask them, “Is this fair, or are you choosing because it’s your friend?” This helps them become aware of bias and think more justly.

title: UNDERSTANDING OPPRESSION
intro: Understanding oppression means recognizing when someone is being treated unfairly, harmed, or denied their rights. It can happen through words, actions, or misuse of power. A believer does not ignore oppression, but understands its harm and stands against it in a wise way. Islam teaches us to protect others and never be a cause of ظلم. Allah does not love oppression and commands justice for all.
quranText: “And those who, when oppression befalls them, defend themselves.” (42:39)
hadithText: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: “Beware of oppression, for oppression will be darkness on the Day of Judgment.” (Sahih Muslim)
storyTitle: Story (From the Life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ)
story: In Makkah, before Islam became strong, there were times when the weak were easily oppressed by the powerful. One of the companions, Bilal ibn Rabah, faced severe ظلم because of his faith. His master would punish him harshly under the burning sun, trying to force him to leave Islam. Despite the suffering, Bilal (RA) remained firm, repeating words of truth with patience. Many people saw what was happening, but few had the courage to act. When the situation became known, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq could not ignore it. He stepped forward and used his wealth to free Bilal (RA), ending his suffering. This was not just an act of kindness, it was standing against oppression. He recognized the ظلم and chose to remove it in the best way he could. Through this, Prophet Muhammad and his companions showed that understanding oppression is not only about seeing it, but about responding to it with courage and compassion.
reflection: Oppression harms people and takes away their rights. When you recognize it, you can choose to stand for justice and help others.
parentTip: Help children identify unfair situations by asking, “Is someone being treated wrongly here?” Encourage them to speak up or seek help when they see ظلم.

title: IDENTIFYING DISHONESTY IN COMPETITION
intro: Identifying dishonesty in competition means recognizing when someone tries to win by unfair means, like cheating, hiding the truth, or breaking rules. Competition should be based on effort and fairness, not tricks or deception. A believer learns to notice such behavior and stays committed to honesty, even when others are not. Allah loves those who compete with integrity and do what is right.
quranText: “Woe to those who give less [than due], who when they take a measure from people take in full, but when they give by measure or weight, they give less.” (83:1–3)
hadithText: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: “Whoever deceives us is not from us.” (Sahih Muslim)
storyTitle: Story (From the Life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ)
story: In Madinah, the marketplace was a place where fairness and honesty were constantly tested. People came to buy and sell, and sometimes the desire to gain more could lead to dishonesty. On one occasion, the Prophet ﷺ passed by a seller who had arranged a pile of grain for sale. From the outside, it looked dry and of high quality. But when Prophet Muhammad placed his hand into the pile, he discovered that the grain underneath was wet. The seller had placed the good grain on top while hiding the lower quality beneath, hoping to make a better sale. It was a form of deception, making the product seem better than it really was. The Prophet ﷺ gently addressed the situation and said, “Why did you not place the wet grain on top so people could see it? Whoever deceives us is not from us.” This moment made it clear that dishonesty is not always obvious. Sometimes it is hidden beneath the surface, and it takes awareness to recognize it.
reflection: Dishonesty in competition may be hidden, but it is still wrong. When you recognize it, you can choose to stay honest and fair.
parentTip: Teach children to value fair play over winning. After games, discuss not just who won, but whether the game was played honestly, helping them recognize and avoid dishonesty.

title: REFUSING TO CHEAT
intro: Refusing to cheat means choosing honesty even when cheating seems easy or tempting. It is standing firm on what is right, even if it means losing or being different from others. A believer understands that success is not just about winning, but about doing things in a truthful and fair way. Allah loves those who stay honest, even when no one is watching.
quranText: “And do not consume one another’s wealth unjustly…” (2:188)
hadithText: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: “Whoever deceives us is not from us.” (Sahih Muslim)
storyTitle: Story (From the Life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ)
story: In Madinah, there was a companion known for his sincerity and strong character, Abdullah ibn Rawaha. He was once sent by the Prophet ﷺ to deal with a group of people regarding matters of wealth and distribution. When he arrived, the people feared that he might judge against them, so they tried to offer him a gift, hoping to influence his decision. It was an attempt to gain advantage in an unfair way. Abdullah ibn Rawaha (RA) immediately understood what they were trying to do. Accepting it would have made things easier and more beneficial for him, but it would also mean compromising honesty. He refused firmly and said that what they were offering was not acceptable. He made it clear that he would judge fairly and truthfully, without taking anything extra. He carried out his responsibility with complete honesty, ensuring that no one was treated unfairly. Through this, Prophet Muhammad and his companions showed that refusing to cheat is not only about avoiding wrongdoing, but about actively choosing fairness even when tempted.
reflection: Cheating may seem like a shortcut, but honesty builds true success. Refusing to cheat makes you strong in character and trustworthy.
parentTip: Create situations where children are praised for honesty, even when they lose. This helps them value integrity over winning and builds a habit of refusing to cheat.

title: ACCEPTING FAIR LOSS
intro: Accepting a fair loss means being okay with losing when the result is honest and just. It means understanding that not winning does not make you less, and that fairness is more important than success. A believer values truth over victory and remains patient and respectful, even when things do not go their way. Allah loves those who accept outcomes with honesty and keep their character strong.
quranText: “…and whoever is patient and forgives, indeed, that is from the matters requiring determination.” (42:43)
hadithText: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: “Look at those who are below you and do not look at those who are above you, for that is more likely to prevent you from belittling the blessings of Allah.” (Sahih Muslim)
storyTitle: Story (From the Life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ)
story: In Madinah, there was a dispute between Zubayr ibn al-Awwam and another man regarding the use of water for their land. Both had a need, and the situation required a fair decision. They brought the matter to Prophet Muhammad. He listened carefully and first suggested a solution that would allow both of them to benefit, showing fairness and consideration. However, the other man was not satisfied and spoke in a way that suggested bias. At that point, the Prophet ﷺ gave a clear and just ruling, granting Zubayr (RA) his full right according to fairness. Even though the outcome was not in his favor, the situation showed that decisions are based on truth, not on personal feelings. The ruling was fair and just, even if it meant one person did not get what they hoped for. This moment taught the companions that accepting a fair decision is part of strong character. Losing something in a just way is better than gaining through unfairness.
reflection: Losing fairly is not a failure. Accepting it with patience shows honesty, respect, and strength of character.
parentTip: After games or competitions, focus on effort and fairness instead of just winning. Help children say, “It’s okay, I’ll try again,” so they learn to accept loss positively.

title: REJECTING DISHONEST ADVANTAGE
intro: Rejecting a dishonest advantage means refusing to gain benefit through unfair or hidden means, even when it is easy and no one may notice. It is choosing integrity over personal gain. A believer understands that true success comes from honesty, not shortcuts. Even when an unfair benefit is offered, they step back and choose what is right. Allah loves those who stay truthful and avoid taking what does not belong to them.
quranText: “And do not consume one another’s wealth unjustly or send it [in bribery] to the rulers…” (2:188)
hadithText: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: “The one who gives a bribe and the one who takes it are both cursed.” (Sunan Abi Dawood)
storyTitle: Story (From the Life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ)
story: In Madinah, a man was appointed to collect charity on behalf of the community. After completing his duty, he returned and said, “This is for you, and this was given to me as a gift.” He tried to separate what he collected officially from what people had given him personally, thinking it was acceptable. When the matter reached Prophet Muhammad, he did not ignore it. He stood before the people and explained the seriousness of this action. He said that if the man had stayed in his home, he would not have received such gifts. They were given to him because of his position, not as personal favors. The Prophet ﷺ made it clear that taking such “gifts” was not right. It was a hidden form of gaining advantage through a role of trust. Through this, the companions learned that even if something appears acceptable on the surface, it must be examined with honesty. Taking advantage of a position or situation for personal gain is not allowed.
reflection: A dishonest advantage may seem small, but it affects your integrity. Choosing honesty over benefit makes you trustworthy and strong in character.
parentTip: When children are offered unfair advantages, guide them to say “No, that’s not fair.” Reinforce that doing the right thing is more important than gaining extra benefits.

title: BEING JUST UNDER PRESSURE
intro: Being just under pressure means doing what is right even when people expect you to do otherwise. Sometimes friends, family, or society may push you to take sides or make unfair choices. A believer stays firm on justice, even when it is difficult or uncomfortable. True fairness is shown when a person does not change their decision because of pressure. Allah loves those who remain just in all situations.
quranText: “O you who believe! Stand firmly for justice, as witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives…” (4:135)
hadithText: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: “The judges are of three types: one in Paradise and two in Hell. The one in Paradise is a man who knows the truth and judges according to it…” (Sunan Abi Dawood)
storyTitle: Story (From the Life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ)
story: In Madinah, a serious case once arose involving a woman from a respected and influential family. She had committed a crime that required a legal consequence. As the matter spread, people became concerned about her status. They felt that if the punishment was carried out, it would affect the honor of her family. Because of this, they tried to find a way to avoid the ruling. They approached Usama ibn Zayd, who was dearly loved by the Prophet ﷺ, hoping he would speak on her behalf and ease the situation. When the request reached Prophet Muhammad, he became serious. He understood that this was a moment where justice was being tested under pressure. If he allowed status or relationships to influence the decision, it would weaken fairness in the community. He made it clear that justice does not change based on who a person is. He said that nations before were destroyed because they allowed the powerful to escape consequences while holding the weak accountable. Then he emphasized that even if someone very close to him were in that situation, the same rule would apply. In that moment, the companions learned that true justice is not easy. It requires strength to stand firm when people expect you to bend. The Prophet ﷺ showed that fairness must remain constant, even under pressure.
reflection: Being just under pressure shows true strength. When you choose fairness over influence, you build trust and honor.
parentTip: Create scenarios where children must choose fairness over friendship, like taking turns or sharing equally. Guide them to do what is right, not just what is easy.

title: PROMOTING FAIRNESS AT HOME
intro: Promoting fairness at home means treating everyone with equal care, giving each person their right, and avoiding favoritism. It includes sharing time, attention, and responsibilities in a balanced way. A believer understands that justice begins at home, and fairness builds trust, love, and respect among family members. Allah loves those who are just in all matters, even within their own families.
quranText: “Be persistently standing firm for Allah, witnesses in justice…” (5:8)
hadithText: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: “Fear Allah and be just between your children.” (Sahih al-Bukhari & Muslim)
storyTitle: Story (From the Life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ)
story: In Madinah, a companion once came to the Prophet ﷺ after giving a special gift to one of his children. He wanted the Prophet ﷺ to witness this gift. When he mentioned what he had done, the Prophet ﷺ asked him, “Have you given the same to all your children?” The man replied that he had not. At that moment, Prophet Muhammad gently but firmly guided him. He told him that it is not right to treat children unequally and that fairness must be maintained within the family. He even refused to be a witness to something that was not just. The companion understood his mistake. What seemed like a simple act of giving had actually created imbalance. The Prophet ﷺ showed that even small differences in treatment can affect hearts. Through this, families learned that fairness at home is essential. When children feel they are treated equally, love and trust grow stronger.
reflection: Fairness at home creates love and trust. When everyone is treated equally, relationships become stronger and happier.
parentTip: Be mindful of equal attention, praise, and rewards among children. Even small acts of fairness help children feel valued and secure.

title: COMPLETING ASSIGNED TASKS
intro: Completing assigned tasks means finishing what you are given with responsibility and sincerity. It shows that you can be trusted and that you value what has been entrusted to you. A believer does not leave things half-done or ignore their duties. Instead, they complete their work carefully, even when it is not easy or when no one is watching. Allah loves those who fulfill their responsibilities with honesty and excellence.
quranText: “O you who believe! Fulfill your commitments…” (5:1)
hadithText: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: “Each of you is a shepherd and each of you is responsible for his flock…” (Sahih al-Bukhari & Muslim)
storyTitle: Story (From the Life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ)
story: After the migration from Makkah to Madinah, there was an important responsibility that needed to be completed. Many people in Makkah had left their valuables with the Prophet ﷺ because they trusted him completely. Even though they were now opposing him, their belongings were still a trust that had to be returned. Before leaving, Prophet Muhammad assigned this responsibility to Ali ibn Abi Talib. He was asked to stay behind in Makkah and return each item to its rightful owner. This was not an easy task. The situation was dangerous, and emotions were high. Yet Ali (RA) carried out the responsibility with care and honesty. One by one, he returned everything that had been entrusted, ensuring nothing was left undone. He did not rush or ignore the task. He completed it fully, just as it had been assigned. Through this, the companions learned that responsibilities are not to be taken lightly. Completing a task, especially when it is entrusted to you, builds trust and shows true character.
reflection: Finishing your tasks shows responsibility and trustworthiness. When you complete what you are given, people learn they can rely on you.
parentTip: Give children small tasks and encourage them to complete them fully. Praise effort and completion so they develop a habit of responsibility. Taking care of belongings

title: TAKING CARE OF BELONGINGS
intro: Taking care of belongings means protecting, maintaining, and using what you have responsibly. It includes not wasting, damaging, or misusing things, whether they belong to you or someone else. A believer understands that everything is a trust from Allah, and how we treat these trusts reflects our character. Allah loves those who are careful and responsible with what they are given.
quranText: “And do not waste. Indeed, He does not like the wasteful.” (2:205)
hadithText: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: “Allah dislikes for you useless talk, wasting of wealth, and asking too many questions.” (Sahih al-Bukhari & Muslim)
storyTitle: Story (From the Life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ)
story: In Madinah, during one of the journeys, the companions of the Prophet ﷺ came across a resting place and decided to stay there for a short while. As they settled, some of them began using the surroundings without much thought, breaking branches and using more than they needed. When Prophet Muhammad noticed this, he guided them gently. He reminded them that even in small matters, a believer should not be careless or wasteful. Everything around them, even nature, was a trust from Allah and should be treated with care. On another occasion, he performed ablution (wudu) using a very small amount of water, showing the companions that even something as simple as water should not be wasted. He did not just teach this through words, but through his own actions. The companions learned that taking care of belongings is not only about personal items. It includes everything Allah has provided, whether it is water, food, or shared resources. Through this, the Prophet ﷺ showed that responsibility is reflected in how carefully a person uses and protects what they have.
reflection: Taking care of things shows responsibility and respect. When you use things carefully and avoid wasting them, you show good character.
parentTip: Encourage children to use only what they need, like water, food, or stationery. Praise careful use so they learn that responsibility includes avoiding waste.

title: DOING HOMEWORK ON TIME
intro: Doing work on time means completing your responsibilities without delay. It shows discipline, respect for time, and reliability. A believer understands that time is a trust from Allah, and delaying tasks without reason can lead to loss and regret. Finishing work on time builds trust and helps a person stay organized and successful. Allah loves those who are careful with their duties and fulfill them properly.
quranText: “By time, indeed mankind is in loss, except for those who believe and do righteous deeds…” (103:1–3)
hadithText: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: “There are two blessings which many people waste: health and free time.” (Sahih al-Bukhari)
storyTitle: Story (From the Life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ)
story: In Madinah, the call to prayer would echo through the streets, calling people to gather for salah. The Prophet ﷺ was always careful about time, especially when it came to acts of worship. Bilal ibn Rabah was given the responsibility to call the adhan. This was not just any task, it had to be done at the correct time so that people could pray properly. He would remain attentive, watching the time carefully and fulfilling his duty without delay. When the time entered, he would immediately call the adhan, ensuring that the community stayed connected to prayer. The Prophet ﷺ emphasized the importance of praying on time and would organize his day around it. His companions learned from this that responsibilities are tied to time, and delaying them without reason is not part of discipline. Through this, Prophet Muhammad showed that doing things on time is part of faith. Whether it is prayer or any responsibility, giving it its proper time shows sincerity and commitment.
reflection: Doing work on time shows responsibility and discipline. When you respect time, you become more trustworthy and successful.
parentTip: Set small time-based tasks for children, like completing homework before a certain time. Appreciate when they finish on time so they learn to value time management.

title: KEEPING PROMISES
intro: Keeping promises means doing what you said you would do. It shows honesty, reliability, and strong character. A believer does not make promises lightly, and once they give their word, they try their best to fulfill it. Breaking promises hurts trust, while keeping them builds respect and confidence. Allah loves those who are true to their commitments.
quranText: “O you who believe! Fulfill your promises…” (5:1)
hadithText: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: “The signs of a hypocrite are three: when he speaks, he lies, when he promises, he breaks it, and when he is entrusted, he betrays the trust.” (Sahih al-Bukhari & Muslim)
storyTitle: Story (From the Life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ)
